steps.tx: **Shock** is acute circulatory failure causing cellular hypoxia despite oxygen delivery, classified as hypovolaemic, cardiogenic, distributive and obstructive. The **cardiac index below two point two L per min per m2** and **mean arterial pressure 65 mmHg** mark shock severity. Global incidence exceeds five point six million intensive care admissions yearly with 30% mortality. Immediate classification directs fluids, vasopressors or pericardiocentesis without waiting for full data.
steps.say: Shock is acute circulatory failure causing cellular hypoxia despite oxygen delivery, classified as hypovolaemic, cardiogenic, distributive and obstructive. The cardiac index below two point two litres per minute per square metre and mean arterial pressure sixty five millimetres of mercury mark shock severity. Global incidence exceeds five point six million intensive care admissions yearly with thirty percent mortality. Immediate classification directs fluids, vasopressors or pericardiocentesis without waiting for full data.

steps.tx: Risk factors include **major haemorrhage**, **myocardial infarction**, **anaphylaxis**, pulmonary embolism and **sepsis** as the leading distributive cause. Trauma accounts for twenty five percent of hypovolaemic admissions and myocardial infarction for 20% of cardiogenic cases. **Tension pneumothorax**, cardiac tamponade and massive embolism cause obstructive shock. Age above 65 years, diabetes and prior heart failure double shock mortality. **Central venous catheters** themselves carry 1 to 2 per one thousand device day infection risk.
steps.say: Risk factors include major haemorrhage, myocardial infarction, anaphylaxis, pulmonary embolism and sepsis as the leading distributive cause. Trauma causes twenty five percent of hypovolaemic admissions and myocardial infarction causes twenty percent of cardiogenic cases. Tension pneumothorax, cardiac tamponade and massive embolism cause obstructive shock. Age above sixty five years, diabetes and prior heart failure double shock mortality. Central lines themselves carry infection risk.

steps.tx: Mechanism centres on **oxygen delivery** falling below consumption, tracked by **mixed venous oxygen saturation below 70%** and lactate above 2 mmol per L. Early phase shows compensatory tachycardia and vasoconstriction, while late phase adds metabolic acidosis, capillary leak and myocardial depression. **Capillary refill above 3 seconds** predicts mortality better than blood pressure alone. Microcirculatory shunting sustains hypoxia even after pressure normalises. **Sequential organ failure** follows uncorrected hypoperfusion.

steps.tx: Classic signs are cold clammy skin, **narrow pulse pressure**, collapsed veins and **oliguria below 0.5 mL per kg per hour** in hypovolaemic shock. Cardiogenic shock shows raised jugular venous pressure, pulmonary crackles and **gallop rhythm**. Distributive shock keeps warm peripheries with **bounding pulse** and low diastolic pressure. Obstructive shock shows distended neck veins with muffled heart sounds in tamponade. **Mottling over knees** predicts 30% excess mortality in shock cohorts.
steps.say: Classic signs are cold clammy skin, narrow pulse pressure, collapsed veins and oliguria below zero point five millilitres per kilogram per hour in hypovolaemic shock. Cardiogenic shock shows raised jugular venous pressure, pulmonary crackles and gallop rhythm. Distributive shock keeps warm peripheries with bounding pulse and low diastolic pressure. Obstructive shock shows distended neck veins with muffled heart sounds in tamponade. Mottling over knees predicts thirty percent excess mortality in shock cohorts.

steps.tx: The **first test** is **bedside echocardiography** with inferior vena cava view and lung sliding, plus **central venous pressure** monitoring and arterial line for pressure. The **gold standard** is **pulmonary artery catheter** measurement of **cardiac output** with 90% accuracy for mixed shock, though less invasive monitors dominate now. **Point of care ultrasound** of veins detects volume responsiveness with eighty five percent sensitivity. **Serum lactate** clearance of 20% per 2 hours confirms resuscitation. **ScvO2 above 70%** guides transfusion thresholds.

steps.tx: First line therapy for hypovolaemic shock is **balanced crystalloid 30 mL per kg** with blood transfusion 1:1:1 ratio for major haemorrhage. **Norepinephrine zero point zero five to 1 mcg per kg per minute** restores **mean arterial pressure 65 mmHg** in distributive shock. **Intramuscular vasopressor 0.5 mg** is the first dose for anaphylaxis followed by infusion. Cardiogenic shock needs **dobutamine 5 to 20 mcg per kg per minute** bridging to revascularisation. Obstructive cause needs needle decompression or pericardiocentesis urgently.

left.title: Fluid responsive shock
points: Stop bleeding or drain sepsis source
Urine output 0.5 mL per kg per hour

right.title: Vasopressor dependent shock
points: Norepinephrine zero point zero five to 1 microgram per kg per minute
Add vasopressin zero point zero three units per minute
Dobutamine when cardiac index stays low

steps.tx: Monitoring escalation includes **dynamic arterial pressure** waveform analysis, hourly urine output and 4 hourly lactate. **Pulse pressure variation above thirteen percent** predicts fluid responsiveness with eighty five percent accuracy. **Transpulmonary thermodilution** and **dilution systems** estimate cardiac output within 10% of catheter. **Bispectral index** targets 40 to 60 during sedation.Daily weight, fluid balance and **extravascular lung water index** guard against overload during resuscitation.
steps.say: Monitoring escalation includes dynamic arterial pressure waveform analysis, hourly urine output and four hourly lactate. Pulse pressure variation above thirteen percent reflects fluid responsiveness with eighty five percent accuracy. Transpulmonary thermodilution and dilution systems measure cardiac output within ten percent of catheter values. Bispectral index targets forty to sixty during sedation. Daily weight, fluid balance and lung water index guard against overload during resuscitation.

steps.tx: Post resuscitation care maintains **mean arterial pressure 65 mmHg**, central venous oxygen saturation above 70% and lactate clearance above 20% per 2 hours. **Procalcitonin** above 2 ng per mL supports bacterial sepsis and de escalation. **Mechanical ventilation** uses 6 mL per kg predicted body weight with plateau pressure below 30 cm H2O. **Renal replacement therapy** starts for refractory acidosis or overload. **Stress ulcer prophylaxis** with proton pump inhibitor 40 mg daily prevents bleeding in 2% of shock patients.
steps.say: Post resuscitation care targets mean arterial pressure sixty five millimetres of mercury, central venous oxygen saturation above seventy percent and lactate clearance above twenty percent per two hours. Procalcitonin above two nanograms per millilitre supports bacterial sepsis and de escalation. Mechanical ventilation uses six millilitres per kilogram predicted body weight with plateau pressure below thirty centimetres of water. Renal replacement therapy starts for refractory acidosis or overload. Stress ulcer prophylaxis prevents bleeding.

steps.tx: Complications include **acute kidney injury** in 40% of shock, **acute respiratory distress syndrome** in 25% and hepatic ischaemia with transaminases rising tenfold. **Disseminated intravascular coagulation** complicates 20% with excess mortality. Cardiac arrest occurs in 15% of refractory distributive shock. Fluid overload causes pulmonary oedema with 30% ventilator days increase. **Critical illness polyneuropathy** affects 30% of long stay shock survivors with prolonged weakness.

steps.tx: Learn the **exam traps**: warm peripheries with bounding pulse mean distributive, cold with narrow pulse mean hypovolaemic or cardiogenic. **Central venous pressure** alone never assesses fluid responsiveness, while **pulse pressure variation** does. **Intramuscular vasopressor** is the drug for anaphylaxis, not intravenous bolus first. **Norepinephrine** is the first vasopressor, not alternatives routinely. **Lactate above 2 mmol per L** with **ScvO2 below 70%** defines ongoing shock despite normal pressure.

steps.tx: **High-yield for the exam** table binds type, sign and drug. Hypovolaemic shock needs **30 mL per kg** fluids and blood. Cardiogenic shock needs **dobutamine 5 to 20 mcg per kg per minute**. Distributive shock needs **norepinephrine zero point zero five to 1 mcg per kg per minute** for pressure 65 mmHg. Anaphylaxis needs **intramuscular vasopressor 0.5 mg**. Obstructive shock needs decompression. Lactate clearance 20% per 2 hours judges response.
